items.title: Holdings is TWO components, nothing else
items.directive: Holdings shows exactly two things. (1) ONE canonical 'All Categories / Total Assets' fixture card that starts at the accounts in play (level L-1), drills to Models / SMAs / Client (L0), then to each L0 item's contents (L1, L2 ...), with the hover preview and the modal pop-up the MDPF card already has. (2) The securities tree map and, under it, the holdings table, both updating from whatever is selected in component 1. Every other card on the tab goes.

quotes.text: flag this, urgent, look here, important. What we are doing for the holdings page is there are two component structures ... That whole flow needs to be contained ... that is one component and drill down modal sequence ... Then two, we have the tree chart, which should display automatically and should update based on what is selected ... And underneath that is the holdings breakdown.
that account level needs to effectively be like L negative 1. It needs to sit before L0, where L0 is the model's, SMA's, client.
if you look at the MDPF underscore one, we already have the exact design for what this needs to look like ... It should be exactly what you see right in that picture.

screenshots.shows: The Total Assets card draws a single grey slice and ONE category tile named for the account's rebalancer strategy; beneath it a second pie and table repeat the same four lines (three models and the client residual) in other colours.
The All-accounts view is a separate pie of the two accounts (near-white and grey slices, outlined labels) and a table, outside the canonical card.
The canonical fixture: one navy card, Total Assets, a filled pie, and three nested tiles Models / SMAs / Client with their share of total.
Hover state: the Models tile expands to a colour-coded bar with Primary and Custom and 'View breakdown'.
'View breakdown' opens the HeroDialog: What it is, How it is derived, a colour bar, the Primary and Custom members with amounts, and a source line naming the data vendors.

should be organized not just by weight. It should be a tuple of weight by asset class. So starting from fixed income, then equity, and so on, following the exact same format that we use in positioning.

both the tree charts and the holdings breakdown should be almost exact copies of what's in positioning. This is not a new build ... The only addition in this case is what you built out with this other and, like, smaller holdings thing that's gray. That's fine. We can keep that.

items.title: Analysis is a three-page, next/back flow: Portfolio -> Analysis type -> Output -> Generate
items.directive: Page 1 SELECT PORTFOLIO: two big cards, Client or Prospect. Client defaults to the client chosen in the top search, or offers a search in its modal if none is chosen; Prospect opens the upload modal (AD-07). Page 2 CHOOSE ANALYSIS: the Overview / Comparison / Multi-Comp cards (AD-08). Page 3 OUTPUT: text inputs only -- title, who the report is for, any other field the output needs; firm follows the user's email (low priority: the beta runs from Global). One obvious Generate. The pages move back and forth freely.

quotes.text: There should be three primary functions here that you just click next, next, next through. The first one is the portfolio cross card ... That should effectively just give them the choice of client or prospect.

if it's client, it will default to whatever client is already selected from the initial search bar. If there is no client selected, then in the modal it will give them the option to search for a client. The alternative button click that they can do here is prospect, which, of course, is going to pull up a card for the CSV or XLSX upload
the third page, which would be essentially a bunch of text inputs ... what is it going to be titled? Who is the client? ... Firm should be automatically selected based on the email.
three clear, effectively, like, pages that you should be able to cursor right and left through

screenshots.shows: Today: Generate shows the three variant cards, 'Client: the client selected above', the account list, 'Holdings snapshot', a collapsed 'Report title, recipient and comparisons', 'Variant Overview (0 comparisons)', a red recipient error on load, a grey Generate and 'No job submitted from this browser yet.'
'Analyze a prospect portfolio instead' is a collapsed line below Generate, not a first choice.

quotes.text: It should be extremely clear where the upload is, that there's no button anywhere that I can see that would clearly delineate that advisors can upload. And when they click upload, they should see instructions on that modal ... And we have a CSV that already is a template that you should be able to find, that should be mentioned somewhere

There is no modal here ... a modal pops up in the standard canonical form, and the modal has the design notes and explanation of what this analysis type is ... there should be a clear indication of which you're selecting here.

we see a lot of scalers and disclosures and charts. Looks like nothing is actually connected from reading those strings, or there's conflicts or missing dependencies ... incomprehensible strings with a green hashtag saying it's supported. I have no idea what that means.

items.acceptance: Each request row reads '<client> -- <analysis type> -- <date> -- <status in words>'; 'needs attention' says what is wrong and what the user can do; a READY request opens the finished report (sections, charts, figures with units) with no codes, hashes or diagnostics on its face; diagnostics, if kept, sit behind one 'technical details' control.
